# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment
The incumbent uses 7 LUTs and meets setup and hold timing, so promotion requires a strictly lower LUT count. The three prior candidates were rejected without improvement: narrowing the counter increased LUT use, changing the comparison left it unchanged, and changing the increment increased it. The current 32-bit counter has an 8-bit repeating sequence; top latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required.

## Hypothesis
Store the complemented 8-bit phase and count downward so the PWM comparison can use the reversed inequality; this may map the counter and comparator to fewer LUTs, and succeeds only if routed LUT use falls below 7 while all verification and timing gates pass.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the `counter` state and its conditional increment with an 8-bit complemented phase register that resets to `8'hFF` and decrements naturally each active cycle. Replace the PWM comparison with the equivalent `phase > ~duty`, keeping `pwm_out` registered and reset to zero. Preserve the existing 256-cycle phase order and output behavior for every duty value; do not add a latency annotation.
